system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Delphi Technologies PLC realized record after the 2017 separation, ~2020-2022 horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at ~2020-2022 (3-5
> years after the ~2017 closing). Within that window the registrant was acquired and
> ceased public reporting; the last standalone audited annual report is for fiscal year
> 2019. This sub-dossier contains no information about how the transaction was structured
> at closing.

## Public-reporting status across the outcome window (feasibility-relevant)
- The separated company became an independent publicly-traded company as Delphi
  Technologies PLC on December 4, 2017; its last standalone annual report on Form 10-K
  covers the fiscal year ended December 31, 2019 (filed 2020-02-13). [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- On October 1, 2020, BorgWarner Inc. completed its acquisition of Delphi Technologies PLC
  by means of a court-sanctioned scheme of arrangement, after which Delphi Technologies
  became a wholly-owned subsidiary of BorgWarner. [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-261833, Form 8-K (event date October 1, 2020)]
- Prior to the effective time the shares had traded on the NYSE under the symbol DLPH; a
  Form 25-NSE (notification of delisting) was filed 2020-10-02 and a Form 15-12B
  (certification and notice of termination of registration under Section 12(b)) was filed
  2020-10-13, ending the company's public reporting. [SRC: SEC accession 0000876661-20-000869, Form 25-NSE] [SRC: SEC accession 0001206774-20-002875, Form 15-12B]
- Consequently no standalone public annual report exists for fiscal years 2020, 2021, or
  2022; the best-documented realized scalars below come from the last standalone Form 10-K
  (FY2019) and the primary filings recording the October 2020 acquisition. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Realized financial record — last standalone audited year (FY2019 vs FY2018)
- Net sales were $4,361 million for the year ended December 31, 2019, down from $4,858
  million for the year ended December 31, 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019), selected financial data]
- Operating income was $141 million in 2019, down from $434 million in 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019), selected financial data]
- Net income was $33 million in 2019, down from $380 million in 2018; net income
  attributable to Delphi Technologies was $17 million in 2019, down from $358 million in
  2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019), selected financial data]

## Documented operational strain and reorganization over the window
- Cost of sales in 2019 was affected by a shift in customer demand from higher-margin
  passenger-car diesel fuel injection systems toward lower-margin GDi fuel injection
  systems, an increase in impairment charges of $22 million related to declines in the fair
  values of certain fixed assets, and $14 million of additional depreciation expense. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- Selling, general and administrative expense in 2019 included an increase in impairment
  charges of $9 million related to certain capitalized information technology assets and a
  real estate operating lease asset. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)]
- As of December 31, 2019 the company reorganized the management reporting structure,
  splitting the former Powertrain Systems segment into three distinct segments (with the
  Aftermarket segment unchanged), stated to "better align our product portfolios and process
  technology expertise." [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)]

## Terminal transaction within the window
- On January 28, 2020 the company announced a definitive transaction agreement under which
  BorgWarner would acquire it in an all-stock transaction, with each Delphi Technologies
  ordinary share to be exchanged for 0.4534 shares of BorgWarner common stock plus cash in
  lieu of fractional shares; this transaction closed October 1, 2020 as described above. [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-261833, Form 8-K (event date October 1, 2020)]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Across the fixed ~2020-2022 window the realized record is bounded: the last standalone
  audited year (FY2019) shows sharply lower net sales, operating income, and net income
  versus the prior year, alongside fixed-asset and IT-asset impairment charges and a
  reorganization of the operating segments; the company was then acquired by BorgWarner on
  October 1, 2020, delisted, and deregistered in October 2020, so no standalone public
  audited outcome exists for FY2020-FY2022. Because the acquirer reports Delphi Technologies
  only within its consolidated results and no separate acquired-business trajectory is
  disclosed here, any post-acquisition standalone financial outcome is coded uncertain (no
  standalone public record). [SRC: SEC accession 0001707092-20-000004, Form 10-K (FY2019)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-20-261833, Form 8-K (event date October 1, 2020)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001206774-20-002875, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
